candidates.exact_span: Radioactivity, Nutrients, and Chlorine, as Total
candidates.computation_change_reason: The phrase 'as Total' groups parameters under a total-analyte basis. Interpreting whether reported dissolved or other speciated measurements must be matched to these rows, converted, or treated as non-comparable changes which limit row applies and whether a numeric compliance comparison is possible.

The section header 'as Total' signals a total-metal analytical basis for the grouped pollutants. A different reading of whether dissolved, recoverable, or valence-specific rows override this grouping would change which numeric limit applies to a given measurement.

The '(irr)' qualifier ties the parameter to an irrigation use context while the row also carries an acute aquatic limit of 0. Interpreting whether irrigation naming, dissolved speciation, or the aquatic column governs changes limit applicability (A), whether monitoring for this form is required (B), and how to classify missing or NODI results for this parameter (C).

The '(NMED SOP)' qualifier ties the parameter to a specific analytical method/definition distinct from other aluminum rows. Whether measurements reported under a different method must be mapped to this row affects limit selection (A), monitoring obligation matching (B), and whether absent or non-SOP results count as adequate evidence (C).

The '(P)' notation marks a priority-pollutant variant of the parameter name. Interpreting whether '(P)' imposes distinct monitoring or limit applicability beyond the all-N/A cells in this table changes which requirements are evaluated (B) and whether a numeric limit comparison is applicable versus report-only (A).

This row is explicitly conditional on sulfate concentration exceeding 500 mg/l. Whether that condition is met for a given monitoring period determines if this selenium limit/monitoring row applies (A,B) and how to classify selenium results or missing data when sulfate is unknown or below the threshold (C).

Valence- and speciation-specific chromium rows coexist with 'Chromium, Total'. Interpreting which row governs when only total chromium is reported, or when speciation is not measured, changes applicable limits (A) and which monitoring forms are required (B).

This dissolved Cr(VI) row is separate from Cr(III) and total chromium rows. Whether Cr(VI) or total chromium measurements must be compared here affects limit applicability (A) and whether Cr(VI)-specific monitoring was required (B).

Dissolved and total mercury rows share a CAS/STORET code but are listed as separate parameters. Interpreting whether reported total mercury may be compared to the dissolved row, or vice versa, changes which limit applies (A) and which monitoring obligation is in force (B).

A dissolved molybdenum row is listed separately from 'Molybdenum, total recoverable' with different STORET codes. Matching reported results to the correct form changes applicable limits (A) and monitoring requirement applicability (B).

The misspelling 'dissovled' versus 'dissolved' affects whether reported measurements and permit parameters refer to the same analyte. Different string matching could change which limit row is selected (A), whether dissolved-manganese monitoring was required (B), and whether missing results for 'dissolved manganese' satisfy evidence for this row (C).

This row contains numeric 5.2 limits in multiple wildlife/aquatic/concentration columns plus distinct mass-load limits. Interpreting which column (concentration vs load, wildlife vs aquatic) is the enforceable discharge limit changes compliance comparisons (A) and which monitoring parameters and units were obligatory (B).

The DIOXIN group header row shows a numeric 0 in the far-right load column while the listed congener 2,3,7,8-TCDD row is all N/A. Interpreting whether the zero applies to dioxin as a class, to load only, or is a formatting artifact changes whether a numeric limit comparison is applicable (A) and how to classify missing dioxin evidence (C).
